ai.description: Barkudia melanosticta is a small, limbless skink reaching 15 cm. It is pale brown with scattered black spots and possesses a shovel-shaped snout and smooth, shiny scales. It belongs to family Scincidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Barkudia melanosticta* is uniquely distinguished by its complete lack of external limbs and a distinct, wedge-shaped snout adapted for burrowing, unlike other Indian skinks.
ai.habitat: *Barkudia melanosticta* inhabits coastal sandy soils and leaf litter within tropical deciduous forests and scrublands, typically at low elevations near the Indian east coast.
ai.behavior: Barkudia melanosticta is a fossorial lizard that spends most of its life burrowing underground, emerging primarily during the monsoon season to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Barkudia melanosticta* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–3 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Barkudia melanosticta* is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily occurring in the coastal plains of Odisha and potentially parts of Andhra Pradesh at low elevations.
